4828.t: From some derivative of Proto-Indo-European *dʰeh₁- (“to do; to set”), and compared in particular to Sanskrit धाक (dhāká, “container”). See also τίθημι (títhēmi, “to place; to put”), from the same root.

4820.t: From Proto-Indo-European *yes- (“to boil, foam”). Compare Sanskrit येषति (yeṣati, “to boil, bubble up”), यसति (yásati, “to froth up, foam”), English yeast.

4843.t: Likely Pre-Greek, and generally connected with κάννα (kánna, “reed”).

4888.t: From Proto-Hellenic *korsā́, a primary verbal noun from Proto-Indo-European *kers- (“to shave”), an s-extension of *(s)ker- (“to cut”), the same root of κείρω (keírō, “to cut, shear, crop”), κόρση (kórsē, “temple (of forehead)”), and κορμός (kormós, “trunk…

4876.t: Thematic transformation of an r/n stem *κεραϝαρ (*kerawar) (< Proto-Hellenic *kerawər), from a verb "to shatter" that was replaced by the related κεραΐζω (keraḯzō), from Proto-Indo-European *ḱerh₂- (“to smash, shatter”).

4830.t: From θύω (thŭ́ō, “to storm; to rage”), with a suffix by analogy with ἄελλα (ắellă, “whirlwind”).

4804.t: From Proto-Hellenic *eurús, from Proto-Indo-European *h₁wérus (“wide”). Compare Sanskrit उ॒रु (urú, “wide; large; spacious”) and Avestan 𐬬𐬊𐬎𐬭𐬎 (voᵘru, “wide”).

4893.t: Proto-Hellenic *kteňňō, from Proto-Indo-European *tḱen- (“strike”), with a *y progressive aspect marker and metathesis of Proto-Indo-European *tḱ- into Proto-Greek *kt- (compare χθών (khthṓn)).

4874.t: From Proto-Indo-European *kh₂ulós or *kawlós (“tubular bone, pipe, stalk”), possibly earlier *kéh₂wl̥, from a root *keh₂- or *kewh₂-, *keh₂w- (“hollow”) (compare κοῖλος (koîlos)); however there are unresolved phonetic problems, such as the lack of…

4825.t: Deverbal adjective from θέω (théō, “to dash, to race; to fly”) + -ός (-ós, an adjectival suffix), with expected o-grade monophthongization of the verbal stem. Compare Θόας (Thóas).

4842.t: From κατα- (kata-, “down”) + μύω (múō, “to close, to shut”).

4891.t: According to Beekes, from Proto-Indo-European *krows- (“push, bump, strike, break”), zero grade *krus-.

4831.t: A loan from Semitic. Compare Hebrew תֵּבָה (tēḇā, “ark, vessel”), Arabic تَابُوت (tābūt).

4834.t: κατα- (καθ-) (“fully”) + ἱδρύω (“make to sit down; settle; found”).

4878.t: Unexplained. The connection with Old Armenian քամեմ (kʻamem, “to press (out)”) is formally possible but it is incompatible with the probable basic meaning of the Greek word, wicker.

4811.t: From εὐ- (eu-, “good”) + ζώνη (zṓnē, “belt, girdle”) and the suffix -ος (-os).

4892.t: The element "-σσ-", as well as the technical meaning, points to a Pre-Greek origin. Previously the word has been compared with Old English crocca (“crock”), Dutch kruik (“jug”) and Middle Irish croccán.

4846.t: From a Semitic source equalling Hebrew קְצִיעָה (qəṣīʿā), Aramaic קְצִיעֲתָא (qəṣīʿătā), from קְצַע (qṣaʿ, “to cut off”), referencing the manner the tree produce is reaped.

4885.t: Frisk assumed that this word and κνώδων (knṓdōn, “projecting teeth on the blade of a hunting spear”), κνώδαξ (knṓdax, “pin, pivot”) go back to a verbal noun *κνωδ- (*knōd-, “tooth, biter, gnawer”), belonging to κναίω (knaíō, “to scrape, scratch”).

4879.t: According to Herodotus, from Phoenician; compare Hebrew קִנָּמוֹן (kinamón, “cinnamon”). The ending was modelled on that of ἄμωμον (ắmōmon, “black cardamom”), or due to folk etymology, on that of ἄμωμος (ắmōmos, “blameless”).

4872.t: From καταλύω (katalúō) + -σις (-sis); also analyzable as κατα- (kata-) + λύσις (lúsis).

4832.t: From Proto-Indo-European *tḱn̥-, zero-grade of *tḱen- (“strike”), with a *y progressive aspect marker and simplification of Proto-Indo-European *tḱ- to *ḱ- before a syllabic nasal (compare χαμαί (khamaí) and Proto-Indo-European *ḱm̥tóm).

4864.t: From κατα- (kata-, “down, thoroughly”) + χρίω (khrī́ō, “to rub, smear; anoint”).
